turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son, feeling a mix of anxiety and determination, told his mother that he would follow her wishes and make sure that all was prepared for his marriage as she desired.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked her husband to ensure that the feast was sufficient for all and that her son and his new wife felt welcome and cared for, emphasizing the importance of family unity.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan quietly that the preparations for the feast were complete and that everything was in place for her son's marriage.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that her husband and son must not neglect the care of her younger son and the maid after she was gone, emphasizing the importance of continuing the family line and supporting one another.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son, his voice trembling slightly, told his mother that he would ensure that his younger brother and the maid were well looked after, just as she wished.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked her husband and son to promise that they would maintain the family's traditions and continue to care for each other, stressing the importance of unity and support in the face of adversity.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son, visibly moved, told his mother and father that he would do everything in his power to uphold their values and protect the family.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked her husband and son to ensure that the wedding feast proceeded without her, telling them that her greatest wish was for her family to be happy and united.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son, his voice soft and filled with emotion, told his mother and father that he would make sure the wedding feast was a celebration of her life and legacy, promising to keep her spirit alive in every aspect of their future.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan and their son that he would do all in his power to ensure her last wishes were fulfilled, reassuring them with a hopeful and determined tone.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother and father that he would do all in his power to make sure the wedding feast was a joyous celebration, keeping his mother's wishes at the forefront of their minds.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told her husband and son that she wished to see the maid married to the second son, ensuring that her family's future was secure and united.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan and their son that he would arrange for the maid to be married to the second son, as it was important to him that her last wishes were honoured.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother and father that he would speak with his new wife and the second son to ensure that the wedding arrangements proceeded smoothly and in accordance with his mother’s wishes.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told Wang Lung and the eldest son that she would assist in any way she could to ensure the wedding arrangements were made with care and respect.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told the eldest son and the maid that he would personally oversee the preparations for the wedding, ensuring everything was done with the utmost care and respect.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told Wang Lung and the eldest son that she would speak with the second son to understand his thoughts and feelings regarding the marriage, ensuring that everyone was content with the arrangement.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told Wang Lung and the maid that he would spend time with his new wife to discuss the details of the wedding and ensure that everything would be arranged to make his mother happy.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung assured the maid and the eldest son that he would do everything in his power to make O-lan's last wish come true, hoping to bring her peace and happiness.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told Wang Lung and the eldest son that she would attend to O-lan, ensuring that she was comfortable and at ease during this difficult time.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she could not speak of dying and please him.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she must die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wed the good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served her, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe her face when she sweated in pain. Now she wanted her son to come home, because she must die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she could die easily, knowing her grandson was stirred into life and a great grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she would see him wed and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung to sit here and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung if everyone had wine and if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot and if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it and the eight fruits.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told her eldest son that she was now content and that he should look to his father and grandfather for guidance. She also instructed her daughter to observe her husband and his ancestors, pointing out the foolish woman in the court as an example of what not to do. O-lan insisted that her children had no duty to anyone else beyond these teachings.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung how that one could feed him and care for him as she did. Beauty would not bear a man sons!
